new_task_1.title: Scope doctest stdlib compatibility shims to affected Python versions
new_task_1.description: Pytest 8.3.0 narrows its doctest monkeypatches so they are only applied on Python versions whose stdlib doctest implementation still needs them. Older interpreters keep the property/wrapper line-number and mock-handling workarounds, while newer Python patch releases defer to upstream doctest fixes instead of overriding those internals.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure doctest collection and line-number reporting stay correct across supported Python versions without continuing to override private stdlib doctest internals once upstream Python releases have fixed the relevant bugs.

expectation.grounded: When building the doctest finder, pytest should install its custom `_find_lineno` workaround only on Python versions where the stdlib implementation is still known to mishandle `@property` and wrapped callables: all versions below Python 3.11, Python 3.11 before 3.11.9, and Python 3.12 before 3.12.3. Pytest should keep its mock-aware `_find` override only on Python versions below 3.10. On newer interpreters, pytest should otherwise rely on the stdlib doctest implementation rather than overriding those methods.
expectation.conceptual: Users should keep receiving corrected doctest discovery behavior on older Python runtimes, while newer runtimes with upstream fixes should no longer be subject to stale pytest compatibility shims.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to version-gating existing doctest compatibility workarounds. Older Python versions must retain the prior fixes for wrapped objects, properties, and mocked objects. Newer Python versions must stop applying only the obsolete overrides rather than changing unrelated doctest collection behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve compatibility where the stdlib still needs help, but minimize pytest's interference with doctest internals once the interpreter itself provides the correct behavior.

behavior: Pytest applies its doctest `_find_lineno` compatibility shim only on Python versions whose stdlib doctest still needs the property/wrapper line-number workaround.
Pytest keeps the mock-aware doctest `_find` override only on Python versions below 3.10.
On newer Python patch releases with the upstream doctest fixes, pytest defers to the stdlib implementations instead of overriding those methods.
The remaining `_from_module` compatibility override continues to be preserved for Python versions below 3.13.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest runs on a Python version where stdlib doctest still mishandles `@property` or wrapped callables, doctest line-number lookup should continue using pytest's compatibility workaround.
When pytest runs on Python 3.11.9 or newer, Python 3.12.3 or newer, or later minor versions with the stdlib fix, it should no longer install the legacy `_find_lineno` override.
When pytest runs on Python versions below 3.10, doctest discovery should continue to use the mock-aware `_find` workaround.
When pytest runs on Python 3.10 or newer, it should rely on the stdlib doctest `_find` behavior instead of keeping the older pytest override.

new_task_2.title: Improve invalid terminal theme diagnostics for code highlighting
new_task_2.description: Pytest 8.3.0 makes terminal highlighting configuration errors more actionable by improving the `PYTEST_THEME` and `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` validation messages. Invalid theme names now point users to the command for listing available Pygments styles, and invalid theme-mode errors now spell out the allowed values while noting that `dark` is the default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users who misconfigure terminal code-highlighting theme environment variables receive clear, actionable error messages that explain how to correct the setting.

expectation.grounded: When Pygments-based terminal highlighting is enabled and `PYTEST_THEME` names an unknown style, pytest should raise a usage error that includes the invalid value and a hint to inspect available styles with `pygmentize -L styles`. When `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` has an invalid value, pytest should raise a usage error that includes the invalid value and states that the only allowed values are `dark` and `light`, with `dark` identified as the default.
expectation.conceptual: Theme-related startup failures should tell users both what went wrong and how to fix it, instead of only reporting a generic validation failure.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to validation and messaging for `PYTEST_THEME` and `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` during terminal formatter setup. It must not alter successful highlighting behavior, and the absence of Pygments should continue to fall back without forcing highlighting errors.
constraints.conceptual: Improve diagnostics without changing how valid theme configuration works or expanding highlighting requirements.

behavior: Invalid `PYTEST_THEME` values now produce an error message that points users to `pygmentize -L styles` for the list of available styles.
Invalid `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` values now report that the allowed modes are `dark` and `light` and explicitly note that `dark` is the default.
Valid theme and theme-mode values continue to work as before.
If Pygments is unavailable, pytest continues to skip terminal highlighting rather than failing solely because highlighting support is missing.
acceptance_criteria: When `PYTEST_THEME` is set to an unknown style and terminal highlighting is initialized, pytest should raise an error mentioning the invalid value and the `pygmentize -L styles` hint.

When `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` is set to an unsupported value and terminal highlighting is initialized, pytest should raise an error mentioning the invalid value and stating that `dark` (default) and `light` are the allowed values.
When `PYTEST_THEME` and `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` are valid, highlighted terminal output behavior should remain unchanged.
When Pygments is not installed, pytest should still fall back to unhighlighted output instead of turning missing highlighting support into a new hard failure.
